newsitem.title: USA: Salomon Brothers names new chief economist.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Brothers names new chief economist.

text.p: Salomon Brothers Inc. said Monday it named Kermit Schoenholtz as its new chief economist and head of global economic and market analysis.
Schoenholtz, who will be based in London, will have the responsibility of directing Salomon's team of economists in New York, London, Tokyo and Hong Kong.
He replaces John Lipsky, who was named as chief economist at Chase Manhattan Bank earlier in the year.

Salomon also said economist Robert DiClemente will assume responsibilty for its U.S. economic research, while Robert Feldman will continue as head of Japanese economic research. Desmond Lachman, based in New York, will run global emerging markets research.
Schoenholtz joined Salomon in 1986, the brokerage firm said. He worked in bond market research in New York before moving to Tokyo in 1988 as director of economic and market analysis.
In April, 1992, he moved to London and became head of Salomon's economic and market analysis team in Europe.
Prior to joining Salomon, Schoenholtz -- with degrees from Yale and Brown Universities -- was a visiting scholar at the Bank of Japan's Institute for Monetary and Economic Studies from 1983 to 1985.
